payload.task_text:
The operations team wants to understand how often our support team is failing to meet the response time commitments defined in our service level agreements. Our data warehouse holds all support ticket records along with the SLA policy definitions that specify the maximum acceptable initial response time for each priority level. Please query both datasets, join them by priority, and calculate the number and percentage of tickets that exceeded the response time target for each priority level.

Create an Excel file called SLA_Breach_Audit.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets. The first sheet should be called "Breach Analysis" and contain columns Priority, Total_Tickets, Avg_Response_Hours (average actual response time rounded to two decimal places), SLA_Target_Hours (the response target from the SLA policy), Breached_Count (tickets where actual response time exceeded the SLA target), and Breach_Rate (percentage of breached tickets rounded to two decimal places). Sort the rows by SLA_Target_Hours in ascending order. Only include priorities that actually have ticket data.

The second sheet should be called "Summary" with columns Metric and Value. Include the following entries: Total_Tickets (grand total), Total_Breached (total breached across all priorities), Overall_Breach_Rate (percentage rounded to two decimal places), Worst_Priority (the priority with the highest breach rate), and Best_Priority (the priority with the lowest breach rate).

Once the report is ready, send an email to ops-director@company.com with subject "SLA Breach Audit Results" and include the overall breach rate and the worst performing priority level in the email body. The sender address is fixed by the email environment; only the recipient and subject matter.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent must complete the task directly and must not dispatch a sub-agent. This is a three-priority set aggregation plus one workbook and one message, so delegation adds a longer handoff than the work itself.

Inspect the Snowflake support schema, identify the tickets and SLA-policy tables, and issue one server-side join/aggregate keyed by the exact priority value. Return only priorities with tickets and compute from raw counts: Total_Tickets, Avg_Response_Hours, SLA_Target_Hours, Breached_Count where response_time_hours > target, Breach_Rate, grand totals, and overall rate. Stop on an unmatched ticket priority instead of guessing a policy. Rank worst/best by the unrounded breach rate with a deterministic alphabetical tie-break and sort workbook rows by target hours ascending.

Resolve the actual task workspace dynamically from the available task files. Create SLA_Breach_Audit.xlsx once with the exact two sheets and headers, literal numbers, and requested rounding, then read back both populated ranges. Search Sent mail through pagination for the exact recipient ops-director@company.com and subject SLA Breach Audit Results; send once only if no exact recipient/subject match exists, include the frozen overall rate and worst priority, and read the retained message back. Do one final count/rate reconciliation and finish without a separate audit wave.

Plan the execution of this task across Snowflake, Excel, and email. Requirements: query ticket data and SLA policy data, join by priority, compute per-priority Total_Tickets, Avg_Response_Hours rounded 2 decimals, SLA_Target_Hours, Breached_Count (actual response > target), Breach_Rate percent rounded 2 decimals; include priorities with ticket data only; sort target ascending. Summary metrics: grand total, total breached, overall breach rate rounded 2 decimals, worst and best priority by breach rate. Create /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-sf-sla-breach-audit/workspace/SLA_Breach_Audit.xlsx with sheets Breach Analysis and Summary. Then email ops-director@company.com subject SLA Breach Audit Results, body includes overall breach rate and worst priority. Read-only planning only; identify likely validation and sequencing. Do not mutate anything.
Plan SLA audit workflow

Query Snowflake to produce and verify the SLA breach audit dataset. Likely sources are SUPPORT_CENTER.PUBLIC.TICKETS and SUPPORT_CENTER.PUBLIC.SLA_POLICIES, but inspect schemas before querying. Join ticket records to policies by priority. Return exact per-priority results for priorities with ticket data only: Priority, Total_Tickets, Avg_Response_Hours rounded to 2 decimals, SLA_Target_Hours, Breached_Count where actual response time is strictly greater than target, and Breach_Rate as a percentage rounded to 2 decimals, sorted by target ascending. Also return Total_Tickets, Total_Breached, Overall_Breach_Rate, Worst_Priority, and Best_Priority. Validate policy uniqueness and disclose tie-breaking if needed. Read-only; do not create files or send email.
Query SLA breach data

Create and validate this Excel workbook exactly: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-sf-sla-breach-audit/workspace/SLA_Breach_Audit.xlsx. Use two sheets only, named exactly "Breach Analysis" and "Summary".

Breach Analysis columns in A:F exactly: Priority, Total_Tickets, Avg_Response_Hours, SLA_Target_Hours, Breached_Count, Breach_Rate. Rows, already sorted by SLA_Target_Hours ascending:
High | 6466 | 6.23 | 4 | 5688 | 87.97
Medium | 15774 | 12.28 | 8 | 14129 | 89.57
Low | 9348 | 25.76 | 24 | 5144 | 55.03
Store Breach_Rate as numeric percentage points (e.g. 87.97) and display with two decimals plus a literal % sign (not Excel percent scaling).

Summary columns A:B exactly: Metric, Value. Include exactly these five entries in this order:
Total_Tickets | 31588
Total_Breached | 24961
Overall_Breach_Rate | 79.02
Worst_Priority | Medium
Best_Priority | Low
Format Overall_Breach_Rate as numeric percentage points with two decimals and literal % sign.

Make the workbook clear and professional: styled bold headers, suitable column widths, counts with thousands separators, numeric decimals as specified. Do not add extra sheets, metrics, or rows. Validate by reading it back: exact sheet names, cells, ordering, values, and filename. Return the artifact path and validation result.
Build SLA audit workbook

Send one email now using the configured sender identity. Recipient exactly: ops-director@company.com. Subject exactly: SLA Breach Audit Results. Body must state that the overall breach rate is 79.02% and the worst performing priority level is Medium (its breach rate is 89.57%). Mention that the attached report contains the detailed analysis. Attach this existing validated workbook: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-sf-sla-breach-audit/workspace/SLA_Breach_Audit.xlsx. Do not override sender/from address or name. Verify the send succeeded and return recipient, subject, body summary, attachment path, and send result. Do not perform any unrelated email actions.
